stories.headline: S&P falls 4.4%, Nasdaq 5.5% in AI rout after midterms; Taiwan has worst week since 1991

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4%, the Dow lost 1,833 points (3.4%) and the Nasdaq composite dropped 5.5%, all three posting their steepest one-day declines since the April 2025 tariff shock.
key_facts.excerpt: The Nasdaq Composite sank 5.5% into correction territory on Thursday, while the S&P 500 fell about 4.4% and the Dow dwindled roughly 1,833 points, or 3.4%... The S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq posted their steepest one-day declines since the April 2025 tariff shock.

key_facts.fact: The selloff more than erased Wednesday's post-election gain, which had been the US stock market's best day in three months.
key_facts.excerpt: The wipeout more than erased the U.S. stock market's gain from the day before, which was its best in three months.

key_facts.fact: Investors feared Democrats would use control of both houses of Congress to slow the data center buildout; the Philadelphia chip index fell 12%, its second-biggest drop on record, while SanDisk lost 22% and Micron, AMD and Marvell each lost 17%.
key_facts.excerpt: Tech -7.3%, Philadelphia chip index -12%, second-biggest fall on record. SanDisk -22%, Micron Technology, AMD, Marvell all -17%. Nvidia -9%... Investors on Thursday were clearly gripped by the fear that Democrats will use their control of both houses of Congress to slow the data center buildout.

key_facts.fact: The Magnificent Seven lost more than $1 trillion in market value, including more than $440 billion at Nvidia, which turned negative for the year at -2.6%.
key_facts.excerpt: The "Magnificent Seven" lost more than $1 trillion in aggregate market cap, with Nvidia leading the way at a loss of more than $440 billion. Nvidia fell more than 9% and turned negative on the year, with its year-to-date fall now at 2.6%.

key_facts.fact: The Nasdaq-100 fell 6.3%, erasing $2.3 trillion in market value.
key_facts.excerpt: The Nasdaq-100 (^NDX) fell 6.3%, erasing $2.3 trillion in market value.

key_facts.fact: About $3 trillion was wiped off S&P 500 firms on Nov. 5; on Nov. 6 Japan's Nikkei closed down 6%, its deepest one-day drop since April 2025, and Taiwan closed down 4.5% and lost 12.2% for the week, its biggest weekly decline since 1991.
key_facts.excerpt: the Nasdaq sank 5.5% and $3 trillion was wiped off S&P 500 firms... Japan's Nikkei slumped 6%, its deepest one-day drop since April 2025... Taiwan stocks closed down 4.5%, recovering somewhat from their early morning slump. For the week, the index clocked a 12.2% decline, its biggest since 1991, LSEG data showed.

key_facts.fact: South Korea's Kospi fell more than 8% at one point, triggering a circuit breaker, before closing down 6%.
key_facts.excerpt: In South Korea, the Kospi index plunged more than 8% at one point, triggering a so-called circuit breaker... The Kospi eventually closed down 6%, with shares in chipmaker SK Hynix falling more than 10%.

key_facts.fact: Asian authorities stepped in: South Korea's finance minister temporarily eased rules on retail investors' leveraged positions, and people told Reuters that Taiwan's finance ministry instructed state-owned banks to support the market.
key_facts.excerpt: South Korean Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il temporarily easing rules on retail investors' leveraged investments. Multiple people told Reuters the Ministry of Finance in Taiwan called senior executives at state-owned banks in the morning and instructed them to support the market.

stories.headline: Trump says Iran decision coming 'very soon' as Tehran sends nuclear proposal through Qatar

key_facts.fact: Trump said on Nov. 5 that the world "will know very soon" whether he will make a deal to end the war or order new strikes to "destroy what is left" of Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: President Trump said Thursday that the world "will know very soon" his decision on whether to make a deal to end the war with Iran, or to order new strikes to "destroy what is left" of the country.

key_facts.fact: Trump met his top national security advisers on Nov. 5, and Axios reported that CENTCOM is finalizing preparations for possible major combat operations but has received no new orders.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump met with top national security advisers Thursday and said a decision on renewed Iran strikes would come soon. CENTCOM is finalizing preparations for possible major combat operations but has received no new orders, Axios reported.

key_facts.fact: A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran sent Washington a nuclear proposal via Qatar, to be discussed only after the US meets seven Iranian demands, and that the US is reviewing it.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran has sent the United States a nuclear proposal via Qatar, to be discussed only after Washington meets Tehran's seven demands, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Thursday. The official... said the US was reviewing the proposal but declined to provide further details.

key_facts.fact: Iran's top security official Mohsen Rezaei said in Russia on Nov. 5 that Iran will neither open the Strait of Hormuz nor negotiate until the seven conditions are met; the demands include lifting sanctions, releasing frozen assets and war reparations.
key_facts.excerpt: "As long as they do not execute our seven conditions, we will neither open the Strait of Hormuz nor have negotiations". Iran has demanded the lifting of US sanctions, the release of frozen Iranian assets and war reparations, among other conditions.

key_facts.fact: Trump called Qatar's emir on Nov. 6 about efforts to end the war; a Qatari framework reported by Axios would have the US lift its naval blockade and release some frozen assets on day one in exchange for IAEA access, with Iran reopening Hormuz on day two. Neither side has accepted any proposal.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the proposal, the United States would lift its naval blockade and release some of Iran's frozen assets on the first day, in exchange for allowing International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) inspectors access... On the second day, Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz... neither side has indicated that it has accepted any of the proposals.

key_facts.fact: The IRGC said two tankers hit mines and caught fire in or near Hormuz, a day after Iranian media reported five tankers and a tugboat on fire; maritime officials have not confirmed these incidents, and Trump has accused Iran of fabricating such attacks.
key_facts.excerpt: There has been no confirmation of any of the incidents from maritime officials, and President Trump has accused Iran of making up such attacks to drive up global energy prices.

key_facts.fact: UKMTO separately said a tanker leaving the strait reported an explosion on Nov. 5 about 16 nautical miles east of Khasab, Oman; the crew was safe and the vessel continued its voyage.
key_facts.excerpt: A tanker reported an explosion on its port side while sailing out of the Strait of Hormuz, 16 nautical miles east of Khasab, Oman, on Thursday, the UK Maritime Trade Operations center said on Friday. The crew was safe and accounted for.

key_facts.fact: An Iranian Army spokesman warned on Nov. 6 that its forces would strike US targets without geographic limits if Washington attacks.
key_facts.excerpt: The Iranian Army spokesman warned on Friday that forces would strike US targets without geographic limits if Washington attacked Iran.

stories.headline: Trump meets Putin envoy and predicts 'big' deal; Kushner sets out goals before Abu Dhabi

key_facts.fact: Trump said he met privately on Nov. 5 with Putin envoy Kirill Dmitriev after a White House event organized by Melania Trump, and declined to disclose what they discussed.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump said he met privately on Thursday with Russian President Vladimir Putin's envoy after the Russian official appeared with representatives from Ukraine at a White House event organized by first lady Melania Trump. Trump would not disclose what he discussed...

key_facts.fact: Trump predicted an agreement that could reach beyond Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: "It's going to be a big agreement, and it's going to involve more than Ukraine ... I could even say it might involve all of Europe."

key_facts.fact: Kushner listed five goals after the Brussels talks: permanent security consultations, reliable crisis communications, greater military transparency, reciprocal measures to reduce escalation risks and a long-term European security framework.
key_facts.excerpt: Kushner said in a social media post that negotiators were exploring five principal goals: permanent security consultations, reliable crisis communications, greater military transparency, reciprocal measures to reduce escalation risks, and an enduring framework for long-term European security and stability.

key_facts.fact: Kushner wrote that no country would hold a veto over another's alliances and that NATO would remain central to European defense; he published no text or timetable.
key_facts.excerpt: "Each country will retain authority over its own security and alliances, and no country would have a veto over another's sovereign choices," Kushner wrote. Nato, he added, would "remain central to European collective defense"... Kushner published no text, no list of the leaders he spoke of and no timetable.

key_facts.fact: Zelenskyy said in an interview aired Nov. 5 that Ukraine wants specific guarantees on how postwar security support would work; the Abu Dhabi talks next week will be the first trilateral peace discussions since February.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskyy says his government is seeking specific guarantees from Western allies on how post-war security support would function... planned three-way talks next week in Abu Dhabi between Ukraine, Russia and the United States, the first trilateral peace discussions since February.

key_facts.fact: The fighting continued during the talks: Russia's Defense Ministry claimed it downed 496 Ukrainian drones overnight, while Ukraine said it stopped 105 of 128 Russian attack drones.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's air defenses shot down or suppressed 105 of 128 Russian attack drones overnight and into early Thursday... Russia's Defense Ministry said Thursday that its forces shot down 496 Ukrainian drones over 13 Russian regions overnight.

key_facts.fact: Russia claimed on Nov. 5 that it struck a cargo ship carrying military supplies in the Black Sea south of Odesa, as strikes on shipping threaten both countries' grain and oil exports.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia's defense ministry on Thursday claimed its forces struck a cargo ship carrying military supplies in the Black Sea just south of Odesa... grain and oil exports from both nations are under threat.

stories.headline: Shield AI to buy radar maker Echodyne for $5.3B, raising $2.5B at a $28.8B valuation

key_facts.fact: Defense company Shield announced on Nov. 5 a definitive agreement to acquire Echodyne in a transaction valued at $5.3 billion, with $4.8 billion paid and issued at closing and up to $500 million contingent on performance targets.
key_facts.excerpt: Of the $5.3 billion transaction value, $4.8 billion will be paid and issued at closing and up to an additional $500 million is contingent on Echodyne meeting agreed performance targets.

key_facts.fact: The $2.5 billion financing comprises a $1 billion Series H at a $28.8 billion post-money valuation, $1 billion in structured equity from Blackstone-managed funds and $500 million in debt arranged by JPMorgan.
key_facts.excerpt: including $1 billion in Series H funding at a $28.8 billion post-money valuation, a $1 billion structured equity investment from funds managed by Blackstone and $500 million in debt financing led by JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as Sole Arranger.

key_facts.fact: The new valuation is more than double the $12.7 billion Shield AI struck in March, when it raised $2 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: That's more than double the valuation the startup struck earlier this year, when it raised $2 billion at a $12.7 billion value in March.

key_facts.fact: Echodyne's radars are built into counter-drone and security systems used in more than 40 countries, and in September it won a contract with a $250 million ceiling from Joint Interagency Task Force 401.
key_facts.excerpt: Echodyne radars are built into hundreds of counter-drone and security systems used by defense, government and commercial customers in more than 40 countries... In September, Echodyne received a contract with a $250 million ceiling from Joint Interagency Task Force 401.

key_facts.fact: Echodyne's new Kirkland, Washington facility, a $40 million investment, will be able to produce about 30,000 radars per year; the acquisition is expected to close in early 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Echodyne recently opened an 86,350-square-foot manufacturing facility, a $40 million investment, which will be able to produce about 30,000 radars per year... The acquisition is expected to close in early 2027.

key_facts.fact: Shield said the financing closes only with the acquisition; Echodyne is its fifth acquisition and marks its first step into dual-use hardware.
key_facts.excerpt: The $2.5 billion financing will be completed when the acquisition closes and won't proceed if the deal falls through, Shield said. Echodyne is Shield's fifth acquisition and its second this year... marks Shield AI's first steps into "dual-use" hardware.

stories.headline: FDA grants J&J accelerated approval for Rybrevant Faspro in advanced head and neck cancer

key_facts.fact: The FDA on Nov. 5 granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro for adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma that progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro (amivantamab and hyaluronidase-lpuj) for the treatment of adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy.

key_facts.fact: In a trial of 102 patients the overall response rate was 42%, against about 20% or less for currently approved therapies; 56% of responders kept their response for six months or longer.
key_facts.excerpt: In an open-label, multicenter clinical trial involving 102 patients with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC, Rybrevant Faspro had an overall response rate of 42%... Of those patients who had a response, 56% had a response lasting six months or longer. Currently approved therapies are associated with an overall response rate of around 20% or less.

key_facts.fact: The FDA called it the first approval in 10 years for patients with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC who had received prior platinum-based chemotherapy.
key_facts.excerpt: This is the first approval in 10 years of a drug for patients with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC who had received prior platinum-based chemotherapy.

key_facts.fact: J&J said the drug is the first dual-targeted therapy approved in this setting, targeting both EGFR and MET, and the approval rests on the Phase 1b/2 OrigAMI-4 trial.
key_facts.excerpt: It is the first approval of a dual-targeted therapy in this setting, simultaneously targeting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)- and mesenchymal-epithelial transition (MET)... tumor response demonstrated in the Phase 1b/2 OrigAMI-4 trial.

key_facts.fact: Continued approval may depend on verification of clinical benefit in the Phase 3 OrigAMI-5 study.
key_facts.excerpt: Continued approval may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in the ongoing confirmatory trial in first-line HNSCC, the Phase 3 OrigAMI-5 study.

key_facts.fact: The subcutaneous injection takes about five minutes, and Reuters said it will compete with Merck's Keytruda and Bristol Myers Squibb's Opdivo; this is its second FDA clearance in a year, extending it beyond lung cancer.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval is the second FDA clearance for Rybrevant Faspro in the past year, expanding the drug's reach beyond lung cancer... can be administered as a subcutaneous injection in about five minutes... will compete with established therapies including Merck's Keytruda and Bristol Myers Squibb's Opdivo.

stories.headline: Reuters: Silver Lake and Saudi PIF held talks to buy game-engine maker Unity at about $25B

key_facts.fact: Reuters reported on Nov. 5 that a consortium including Silver Lake, which owns about 8% of Unity, and Saudi Arabia's PIF approached the company in recent weeks and discussed a valuation of about $25 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Silver Lake, which already holds roughly 8% of the game-engine company, and the PIF approached Unity in recent weeks, the sources said... The buyer group discussed a valuation of about $25 billion in recent weeks.

key_facts.fact: The valuation was discussed before Unity's latest earnings lifted its market capitalization to about $21.5 billion; Unity is working with an investment bank to evaluate its options.
key_facts.excerpt: The investor group discussed a valuation of about $25 billion before Unity's latest earnings report lifted its market capitalization to roughly $21.5 billion, the report said. Unity has engaged an investment bank to evaluate its options following the approach.

key_facts.fact: Unity shares rose nearly 15% in the regular session on Nov. 5 and a further 6.6% to $52.04 in extended trading after the report.
key_facts.excerpt: Unity shares jumped 6.6% to $52.04 by 19:16 ET after surging nearly 15% in the regular session.

key_facts.fact: A deal is not certain and terms could change; Unity declined to comment, and Silver Lake and PIF did not immediately respond to Reuters.
key_facts.excerpt: A deal is not certain, and the proposal — including any terms — could still change, according to the sources. Unity declined to comment. Silver Lake and the PIF did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.

key_facts.fact: Silver Lake and PIF were also part of the group that took Electronic Arts private for about $55 billion in a buyout completed in August, and Silver Lake CEO Egon Durban sits on Unity's board.
key_facts.excerpt: Silver Lake and Sadia Arabia's PIF were recently involved in the acquisition of Electronic Arts in a deal valuing the company at around $55 billion. The buyout, which was completed in August... Silver Lake CEO Egon Durban also sits on Unity's board.

stories.headline: EU says TikTok's algorithm breached DSA by trapping users in harmful 'rabbit holes'

key_facts.fact: The European Commission accused TikTok on Nov. 6, in preliminary findings under the Digital Services Act, of failing to stop its recommendation algorithm from drawing users into "rabbit holes" of content about sadness, self-harm and body image.
key_facts.excerpt: The European Commission accused TikTok on Friday of failing to prevent its recommendation algorithm from drawing users into "rabbit holes" of content about sadness, self-harm and body image.

key_facts.fact: EU officials said it is the first time regulators there have directly challenged the engagement-based recommendation system of a major social platform and, to their knowledge, the first enforcement action of its kind worldwide.
key_facts.excerpt: European officials said their findings were the first time EU regulators have directly challenged the engagement-based recommendation system of a major social media platform, and, to their knowledge, was the first enforcement action of its kind worldwide.

key_facts.fact: The findings are not final; TikTok can challenge them, and confirmed violations could bring a fine of up to 6% of annual global revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: The findings are not final and TikTok has a chance to review the Commission's evidence and challenge its findings. If the DSA violations are confirmed the company could face a fine of up to 6% of its annual global revenue.

key_facts.fact: Investigators deliberately focused on videos that were neither illegal nor against TikTok's rules, saying that trends such as "what I eat in a day" and "SkinnyTok" become damaging through repetition, particularly for young and vulnerable users.
key_facts.excerpt: investigators deliberately focused on videos that were neither illegal nor against TikTok's own rules... Citing trends including "what I eat in a day" and "SkinnyTok," officials said the legal content could appear harmless in isolation but became damaging through repetition.

key_facts.fact: The Commission said TikTok identified some of the issues in its own risk assessments but failed to analyze the risks properly or set safeguards, and that its "dispersion" techniques to diversify the feed are ineffective.
key_facts.excerpt: Brussels said TikTok had identified some of the issues it was flagging in its own risk assessments, but that its investigators found the company had failed to properly analyze those risks and set appropriate safeguards... the platform's "dispersion" techniques to diversify the feed are ineffective.

sources.title: EU accuses TikTok of trapping users in harmful 'rabbit holes'
